free_text: The 82-year-old male has a PSA of 4.7 and a cT1c diagnosis with a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone. Histology confirms Gleason 3+3 (ISUP Grade Group 1) with perineural invasion. The management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential benefit of treatment against the patient's age and comorbidities. The trade-off involves managing the risk of progression versus the risks associated with active treatment in this elderly patient.
